newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: BEAZLEY ON SUPERANNUATION SURCHARGE
The Federal Opposition says the Government's facing intense legal problems with many of its new proposals.
This follows claims the Treasurer's proposed 15 per cent superannuation surcharge on high income earners is unconstitutional, and just another tax.
Mr Beazley says he doesn't believe a further tax on high income superannuation recipients is a bad thing.
But he says Treasurer Peter Costello is continuing to mislead the public by insisting the surcharge is not a tax.
The Opposition leader has also accused the Government of incompetence over the issue.
NSW POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH DISBANDED
Police Commissioner Peter Ryan has disbanded the New South Wales Special Branch, following evidence given to the Police Royal Commission.
Mr Ryan has begun a special review of the roles and responsibilities held by Special Branch.
Some operational roles undertaken by Special Branch such as VIP protection and security assesments would continue for the time being.
Mr Ryan says can't comment further pending evidence before the Royal Commission.
WORKPLACE AGREEMENTS UNVEILED TODAY
ACTU President Jennie George predicts workers will soon become disadvantaged under the Federal Government's new Australian Workplace Agreements, coming into effect today.
Ms George says once workers cash in entitlements like sick leave and annual leave for extra pay under individual contracts, there'll be people falling under the floor of the disadvantaged award test.
Industrial Relations Minister, Peter Reith, says there was a need to get past an effective veto operated by the unions.
He says the new system works at the choice of the parties, completely non-union and outside the Industrial Relations Commission.
AUSTRALIA/INDONESIA DEAL ON MARITIME BOUNDARIES
A maritime boundaries agreement between Australia and Indonesia will be signed in Perth on Friday after 25 years of negotiations.
The agreement sets out seabed boundaries and exclusive economic zones and will be signed by Indonesia's Foreign Minister, Ali Alatas, and his Australian counterpart Alexander Downer.
It covers boundaries stretching three-thousand kilometres from Java to the Gulf of Carpentaria, and between Java and the Australian territory of Christmas Island.
The agreement means all maritime boundaries between Australia and Indonesia will be covered by treaties.
The deal doesn't change the Timor Gap Treaty for the joint development of oil and gas resources lying between Australia and Timor.
TWO MISSING NEAR PNG AFTER BOAT SANK
US forces in Queensland for Operation Tandem Thrust have helped search for two people missing in waters west of Bougainville after the ship they were on sank.
The Australian Maritime Rescue Co-ordination centre says the 70 metre ship, the Pera, was carrying cargo from Townsville to Papua New Guinea when it capsized in bad weather on Monday.
Yesterday aircraft were dispatched from the USS Independence to assist in the search and so far only six of the eight people missing have been rescued.
The Rescue Co-ordination Centre says all vessels in the area have been alerted.
SHIP TO RETURN TO PORT AMID FIRE FEARS
A cargo ship will return to Port Adelaide, because of a fire in one of its containers.
16-hundred tonnes of sheep pellets on board the Mawahi Tobak will be unloaded.
Bill Dwyer, of the Metropolitan Fire Service, says a gas will be used to cool the fire.
The ship was on its way to New Zealand when the captain noticed that the load was heating up.
It was forced to return to Outer Harbour, near Port Adelaide, last night.
Mr Dwyer says it's a big problem and every precaution is being taken.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
